technical-data.invention-title: DISMOUNTABLE CHAIR CONSISTING OF TWO FRAMES
CHAISE DEMONTABLE COMPOSEE DE DEUX CADRES

addressbook.name: TOMAT S N C DI TOMAT FRANCO &
TOMAT S.N.C. DI TOMAT FRANCO & C.

abstract.p: Chair to be assembled in two opposite frames (1, 2) jointable in a detachable way, in which: each of said two opposite frames (1, 2) has, at least one middle strong cross-piece at the seating height (12) in which at least two spaced transversal notches (120), having dimensions suitable to housing a metal plate with a threaded hole (4), are provided, said cross-pieces internally are transversally holed in correspondence of said plate hole axis (4); a bearing seating frame (3) supplied with at least two opposite sides (32) with transversal holes coinciding with the previous ones is provided and; at least four threaded screws (5) for clamping, in said coinciding holes, said opposite frames (1, 2) with said bearing seating (3), by the screwing from the inside on said metal plates (4) of said screws (5) are provided.

L'invention concerne une chaise formée à partir de deux cadres opposés (1, 2), lesquels peuvent être assemblés de manière détachable de sorte que: chacun de ces deux cadres opposés (1, 2) est muni d'au moins une traverse intermédiaire solide située au niveau de la hauteur (12) de l'assise, deux encoches transversales espacées (120), dont les dimensions leur permettent de loger une plaque métallique avec un orifice fileté (4), étant par ailleurs prévues, et un orifice transversal, correspondant à l'axe (4) de l'orifice de cette plaque, étant pratiqué sur l'intérieur de ladite traverse; un cadre d'assise support (3) présentant au moins deux cotés opposés (32) dont les orifices transversaux coïncident avec les orifices susmentionnés; et au moins quatre vis filetées (5) permettant de fixer, par l'intermédiaire desdits orifices coïncidant, les cadres opposés (1, 2) et le cadre d'assise support (3), ces vis (5) étant vissées depuis l'intérieur des plaques métalliques.

description.p: DESCRIPTION DEMOUNTABLE CHAIR CONS I STING OF TWO FRAMES

Technical Field The present invention has for object a chair to be assembled in two frames jointable in a detachable way. Background Art In prior art chairs to be assembled in two frames for instance (front legs frame and rear legs frame which extends upwards with the back, otherwise laterally opposite frames) jointable in a detachable way are kn o w n . The jointing systems are various using squares or dowels shrouded in the wooden uprights or cross-pieces and tie screw means for the clamping. Drawbacks The present solutions are complex, expensive and are characterised by a limited strength so that often a loosening or breakage danger in the jointing areas occurs. Purpose of the invention The purpose of this invention i s that of obviating the above mentioned drawbacks. Essence of the invention The problem is solved as claimed by a chair to be assembled in two opposite frames jointable in a detachable way, characterised in that: - each of said two opposite frames has, at least one middle strong cross- piece at the seating height in which at least two spaced transversal notches having dimensions suitable to housing a metal plate with a threaded hole, being said cross-pieces internally transversal ly holed in correspondence of said plate hole axis, are obtained;
- a bearing seating frame supplied with at least two opposite sides with transversal holes coinciding with the previous ones is provided and, - at least four threaded screws for clamping, in said coinciding holes, said opposite frames with said bearing seating, by the screwing from the inside on said metal plates of said screws are provided Thus a chair completely detachable and stackable in a flat package with minimum bulk is obtained Advantageously the opposite frames consist of one frame making up the front legs and one frame making up the real legs with an extension towards the back's top As much advantageously said frame seating is an under-frame seating to which an interchangeable seating is fixed In alternative said frame seating is integrated with the seating Advantageously said frame seating has a system foi fixing to said opposite frames by means of four pins or tongues which fix into the respective uprights of said opposite flames Thus a stronger and safei fixing against the danger of the foui sci ews loosening is obtained As much advantageously said sciews are opposite thi eading sci ews and whi le on a side they lock-screw with said plates up to the threading end, substantially for the plates thickness, on the othei they house in engagement a nut with eventual washei for completing the clamping Thus the danger in the bolt use, of clamping by screwing beyond the plate thickness with the risk of breaking the cross-piece for the sci t w protruding beyond the plate thickness is avoided Description of at least one form of invention embodiment These and other advantages wi l l appeal from the f ol lowi ng description of a prefeπ ed solution of embodiment, with the aid of the
enclosed drawings, whose details are not to be considered as limiting but only as examples Figure 1 is a view of the assembled chair in cross section to the seating height, showing the assembling system Figure 2 is an enlarged view in cross section on the vertical plane showing the clamping system by tie-screw with the metal plate Figure 3 is a perspective view of metal plate, washer, tie-screw and clamping nut As it can be seen from the above shown figures, with 1 and 2 the opposite frames to be assembled are indicated Each frame has a cross-piece 12, 22 at the seating height which i . fixed by tonguing or lock-pins to the respective uprights which make up the rear legs and eventual back extension for the rear frame and only legs for the front fiame ( 1 1 ,21 ) The frame seating 3 has a quadiangulai shape with four sides (31 ,32) locked to one another by a pin and stiffened by a central cross-piece (33) eventually holed (330) for the uppei fixing of the interchangeable seating (not shown) Obviousl) the seating might also be integi ated with this frame This frame has four lock-pins on the corners (L) for the fixing w itli the opposite frames ( 1 ,2) The cross-pieces of the opposite frames ( 12,22) have some notches ( 120) for housing a metal plate with threaded hole (4) and the assembling and fixing occurs by four tie-sciews as claimed As it may be noticed from figure 3 said screw is substantially a stud- bolt having a threading depth equal to the thickness of the plate (4) so to be locked into it The clamping completion wi ll be carried out from the inside by means of
nut and washer (6,6' ). Thus the clamping can be carried out as much as necessary with no danger of breaking the cross-piece because the screw will never exit from the plate's other side.

claim.claim-text:
Claims 1 . Chair to be assembled in two opposite frames ( 1 ,2) jointable in a detachable way, characterised in that: - each of said two opposite frames ( 1 ,2) has, at least one middle strong cross-piece at the seating height ( 1 2) in which at least two spaced transversal notches ( 120), having dimensions suitable to housing a metal plate with a threaded hole (4), ids provided, said cross-pieces are internally transversally holed in correspondence of said plate hole axis (4); - a bearing seating frame (3) supplied with at least two opposite sides (32) with transversal holes coinciding with the previous ones is provided and ; - at least four threaded screws (5) for clamping, in said coinciding holes, said opposite frames ( 1 ,2) with said bearing seating (3), by the screwing from the inside on said metal plates of said screws are further provided . 2. Chair according to the previous claim, characterised in that the two opposite frames ( 1 ,2) consist of one frame making up the front legs and one frame making up the rear legs with extension towards the back's top. 3. Chair according to claim 1 and/or 2, characterised i n that said frame seating (3) is an under-frame seating. 4. Chair according to claim 1 and/or 2, characterised in that said frame seating (3) is integrated with the seating. 5. Chair according to claim 1 and/or 2, and 3., characterised in that said frame seating (3) is an under-frame seating with central cross-piece (33) holed (330) for the upper fixing of an interchangeable seating. 6. Chair according to any of previous claims, characterised in that said frame seating (3) has a system for fixing to said opposite frames ( 1 ,2) by means of four pins or tongues (L) which fix into the respective uprights
(1 1 -21 ) of said opposite frames (1 ,2). 7. Chair according to any of previous claims, characterised in that said screws (5) are opposite threading screws and while on a side they lock- screw with said plates up to the threading end, substantially for the plates thickness (4), on the other they house in engagement a nut (6) for completing the clamping.
